prompt:
Use case: style-transfer. Redraw the single copper coin in image 1 as rough hand-painted anime game-item art. Image 1 is the EDIT TARGET and supplies the exact coin, embossed emblem, round shape, mild oblique front view and composition. Images 2–4 are ONLY drawing-style references for broad opaque brushwork; never copy their characters, costumes, props or text.

One substantial round copper coin, centered on a square transparent canvas with generous clear margins, filling about 70 percent of its width. Keep the original near-frontal slightly tilted view, thick raised outer rim and recessed circular inner border, small irregular worn notches along the rim. Preserve the face's original simple embossed leaf-and-crossbar geometric emblem, with the same placement and orientation; group it into a small number of broad readable raised shapes. Keep one coin only, no pile, no stack. Warm muted copper-red and burnt sienna form the main metal body; broad cool smoky plum-gray shadows and a few short pale warm highlights reveal the raised rim, thickness and relief. Preserve the dark relief shadow without drawing dense engraved lines. The main coin face has a handful of connected large color planes and substantial quiet surface.

Rough hand-painted anime color study: large connected opaque masses, a few wide curved directional swipes and blunt dabs, decisive handmade hard shadow edges, broken stroke endings and selective unfinished areas. Stroke shapes follow the circular rim and broad metal turns. Clearly painted metal, controlled highlights and matte quiet midtones, not polished photoreal or glossy 3D. Replace the old fine scratches and thin edge chatter with a few purposeful broad worn marks. No microscopic texture, dense dent noise, tiny facets, all-over grain/canvas filter or airbrushed gloss.

Genuinely transparent alpha everywhere outside the coin. No black or white background, no brush swatch, ground shadow, halo or drawn checkerboard. No new objects, sparks, characters, letters, numbers, currency denomination, text, frame, watermark or UI. Keep the original nonlinguistic emblem.
